chose: Two of the owner's rulings of 2026-11-21, as built. (1) A screen in an essay is never full-bleed, and its caption sits below it, never over the app's own screen. Every whole screen, a snip with no parts named or a clip frame, is drawn by the screen-zoom composition with no stops (wholePicture). It holds the phone in the room above the frame's foot, where the captions draw, on the series' ground, as large as fits there. No size is aimed at: the foot is the caption band the recorder gives (zoomFoot, captionSpace's tallest band), and a silent essay keeps the whole frame. A clip frame is read as a screen of its PNG's own size, scale 1. (2) #3137, option (b): a row of the release APK's controls is its tab bar only when it sits at the foot of what the app draws (its lowest edge within ROW_PX of the app's lowest edge) or one of its tabs is selected. The width rule (BAR_SPAN) is gone. tabBar is pure, in lib/snips, and tested.
options: whole screens through screen-zoom with no stops; the bar by its foot or a selected tab
whole screens as plain stills fitted into the frame; the bar by its span
a device-frame composition of its own
gray: The owner decided what is seen (not full-bleed, the caption below the screen) and which signal finds a bar. How each lands in code is a choice: reusing screen-zoom rather than a still or a new composition, and reading 'the bottom edge' as the app's own lowest edge rather than the screen's.
